title: Bài báo ngắn
text:
LOCAL BAKERY RISES TO NATIONAL FAME

Greenhill (May 22) — Just five years ago, Rosa Delgado was selling bread from a single stall at the Greenhill farmers' market. Today, her company, Rosa's Oven, supplies more than 300 supermarkets across the country.

The turning point came in 2023, when a food blogger's video about her sourdough loaf attracted two million views in a week. "Overnight, we had more orders than we could bake," Ms. Delgado recalled. "I had to decide: stay small or grow fast."

She chose growth — but carefully. Rather than opening her own factories, she partnered with three family-run bakeries in nearby towns, training their bakers in her methods. This allowed production to triple while keeping the handmade quality that made her famous.

Rosa's Oven will open its first overseas location in Singapore this fall. Asked for her advice to small business owners, Ms. Delgado laughed: "Make something worth talking about. The talking, these days, takes care of itself."

title: Bài báo: xu hướng văn phòng
text:
THE QUIET RETURN OF THE OFFICE LIBRARY

Business Trends Weekly (October issue) — Five years ago, office designers could not knock down walls fast enough. Open floor plans promised collaboration, spontaneity, and — not least — lower costs per desk. Today, a growing number of companies are quietly rebuilding what they tore down, one bookshelf at a time.

The newest feature in workplace design is the "library zone": a carpeted, phone-free room where conversation is limited to a whisper. At software firm Datawheel, the library seats thirty and is booked solid by ten each morning. "Our engineers asked for it by name," says workplace director Irene Kovacs. "They didn't want more meeting rooms. They wanted somewhere to think."

Research supports the shift. A 2025 university study tracking 1,200 office workers found that those with access to designated quiet areas reported 23% fewer errors in detail-heavy tasks and, perhaps surprisingly, rated their teams as MORE collaborative — not less. The authors suggest that when deep-focus work has a protected home, meetings become shorter and more purposeful.

The trend has its skeptics. Retrofitting quiet rooms is expensive, and some managers worry the spaces simply hide employees from oversight. But with several major insurers and two government ministries announcing library zones this quarter, the whisper, it seems, is getting louder.

title: Bài báo: giờ làm 4 ngày/tuần
text:
FOUR DAYS, FULL PAY: LOCAL FIRMS JOIN THE SHORTER-WEEK EXPERIMENT

Harbor City Business Journal — When Meridian Insurance announced last spring that its 300 employees would work four days a week for the same salary, competitors predicted chaos. Eighteen months later, the company reports its strongest customer-satisfaction scores in a decade — and its lowest staff turnover ever.

Meridian is not alone. According to a survey by the Harbor City Chamber of Commerce, one in five local employers now offers some form of compressed schedule, up from one in twenty just three years ago. The catch? Success appears to depend less on the calendar than on the meeting room. "Companies that simply squeezed five days of meetings into four failed quickly," says labor researcher Dr. Elsa Moreau. "The ones that thrived cut internal meetings by half or more before touching the schedule."

Not every industry finds the shift easy. Restaurants, hospitals, and logistics firms — where customers expect seven-day service — must hire additional staff to cover the gaps, an expense small businesses cannot always absorb. Meridian's chief executive, Priya Raman, acknowledges the model has limits, but she is blunt about the results in her own office: "We measure output, not hours. Output went up."

Dear Ms. Oyelaran,

Thank you for the detailed video you sent; it made the problem easy to identify. — [1] —

The noise you describe comes from the drive coupler, a small plastic part that wears down after heavy use. It is the single most common repair on the KB-40. — [2] — Because your blender is fourteen months old, it falls outside the twelve-month warranty, and normally a replacement coupler costs $18 plus shipping.

However, our records show that you registered the product within a week of purchase, which extends your coverage by six months at no cost. — [3] — I have therefore arranged for a free coupler to be sent to you today; it should arrive within four working days.

The part clips on by hand and takes about two minutes to fit. — [4] — If you would rather not attempt it, any Kestrel service point will fit it free of charge.

title: Bài báo: chợ đêm hồi sinh khu phố cổ
text:
OLD QUARTER NIGHT MARKET DRAWS CROWDS — AND NEW TENANTS

By Ingrid Halvorsen

When the Old Quarter night market reopened last spring after an eight-year gap, the city council expected a modest weekend attraction. — [1] — Eighteen months later, the market runs four nights a week and counts 140 stalls, more than double the original plan.

The effect on the surrounding streets has surprised even its supporters. — [2] — Eleven shopfronts that had stood empty on Vasa Street are now occupied, seven of them by traders who began at a market stall and outgrew it. Commercial rents in the quarter have risen about twelve percent, a figure that worries some longtime residents.

"A stall costs a fraction of a lease, so you can test whether people actually want what you make," said Bui Thanh Ha, who sold ceramics at the market for a year before opening a shop two streets away. — [3] — Her rent is now four times her old stall fee, but her weekday trade covers it.

Not everyone is celebrating. Residents of the narrow lanes behind the market have complained about noise and rubbish, and the council has agreed to end trading at ten thirty rather than midnight from January. — [4] — Market manager Osei Boateng says the earlier finish will cost traders perhaps eight percent of their takings, but calls it "the price of staying welcome."

text:
MEMORANDUM

To: All staff, Ellis & Frome LLP
From: Rosalind Ferreira, Chief Operating Officer
Date: 3 June
Subject: Hybrid working — confirmed arrangements from 1 July

Following the three-month trial and the feedback session in May, the partners have approved the arrangements below. They replace all previous guidance.

Core office days. Every team must be in the office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. These are the days we schedule client meetings, training and team reviews, so please do not book leave-in-lieu on them without your team leader's agreement.

Remaining days. You may work from home on Mondays, Thursdays and Fridays. Team leaders may ask for one additional office day per month for planning; they will give at least a week's notice.

Desks. With fewer people on site each day, we are moving to bookable desks on floors 4 and 5. Floor 6 keeps assigned desks for staff who requested them on health grounds. Booking opens fourteen days ahead through the workplace app.

Equipment. Everyone working from home may claim up to £250 towards a chair or monitor, once every three years. Broadband costs are not covered.

What has changed since the trial? Two things. The trial allowed one core day; we have moved to two after most teams said one was not enough to see each other. And the equipment allowance, which was £150, has risen.

Questions go to your team leader first, then to me.

CITY OF DUNMORE — SHOPFRONT IMPROVEMENT GRANT

The city will fund up to 60% of the cost of exterior improvements to ground-floor businesses on Harbour Road and Mill Lane, to a maximum of $6,000 per property.

Eligible work: signage, awnings, exterior painting, window repair, accessible entrances.
Not eligible: interior fittings, furniture, security cameras, roof work.

Conditions
• The business must have traded at the address for at least one year.
• Two written quotes must accompany the application.
• Work must be completed within six months of approval.
